candidate_sentences.reason: Matches evidence that heat makes rails expand and gaps close in summer (heat: expand; gaps: gaps close). Drawable with rail_yard and rail_joint:expand (nearly closes).
Supported by heat-driven expansion and existence of small joint gaps that close (heat; gaps). Drawable via rail_joint:expand.
Evidence says expansion generates forces that try to push track out of shape, leading to lateral movement/buckling (forces). Drawable with rail_joint:buckle (shove sideways).
Buckling/kinking from heat-induced forces is stated (heat; forces). Drawable with rail_joint:buckle (kinks).
Gaps at joints close as rails expand (gaps; heat). Drawable via rail_joint:expand.
In cooler times rails contract and gaps open (gaps). Evidence also notes contraction; 'stays open' is consistent with winter (forces mention contraction). Drawable via rail_joint:expand (shorter).
Same mechanism repeats: heat -> expansion -> next gap closes (heat; gaps). Drawable via rail_joint:expand.
When gaps are fully taken up, compressive forces can push track sideways (forces; heat). Drawable via rail_joint:buckle.
Long continuous lengths accumulate compressive force causing buckling (forces). Drawable with rail_joint:buckle.
Evidence says many stretches today still use joint gaps to handle expansion; rails on those tracks expand (gaps). Drawable via rail_joint:expand.
Joints leave a space; rails expand and close that space (gaps). Drawable via rail_joint:expand.
Heat-driven expansion closes the space (heat; gaps). Drawable via rail_joint:expand.
Cooling contraction re-opens the space (gaps). Drawable with rail_joint:expand (shorter).
Older jointed track left gaps because rails grow; this is exactly what the sources describe (gaps; heat). Drawable via rail_joint:expand.
With no room for expansion, compressive forces cause buckling (heat; gaps; forces). Drawable via rail_joint:buckle.
Forces can push the line sideways so it kinks (forces). Drawable via rail_joint:buckle (kink).
Gaps keep rail ends separated while accommodating growth (gaps). Drawable via rail_joint:expand.
Modern CWR uses fastenings (clips/anchors) to restrain expansion and keep original length (modern). Drawable in rail_yard context; rail_joint has 'clips'/'anchors' in vocab.
CWR rails 'want' to lengthen but are held near their set stress length by fastenings (modern). Drawable in rail_yard with rail_joint imagery of rails.
Historically, gaps were needed to prevent kinks/buckles from thermal growth (gaps; heat; forces). Drawable via rail_joint:buckle or expand illustrating the concept.
